close: In a crisis, people look across the room and find you already steady.
Most of your life happens between emergencies, and you are only half there for it.
Your steadiness leaves them little room to steady themselves.
A stuck room starts moving again the moment you walk in.
Your own week fills up with other people's problems.
Around you, people rarely get to test their own judgement.
The jobs others drop halfway are the ones you see through.
Your body pays for the hard way long after the job is done.
With you at the front, the group finishes what it started.
Your work arrives whole, and it answers the doubters by itself.
Ideas that were yours first end up with other people's names on them.
Those close to you meet the work at the end and miss the making of it.
People always know where they stand with you.
Part of you wanted that welcome too.
Your honesty reaches them whole, and some of it stings.
The people who come after you inherit a rule that works.
On paper, you look like trouble.
The rule you found pointless was somebody's floor.
What you learn this way goes deep and stays put.
Underneath sits a wish to owe nobody for what you know.
Whoever learns from you gets the answer and misses the road to it.
Very little gets past you, least of all what people leave unsaid.
You end up alone with hunches nobody else can see.
Talking to you, people get answered before they have said their piece.
Ideas come back from those hours finished and fully yours.
That hour is the one stretch of time that belongs only to you.
The people waiting on you never know when to expect you back.
By the time others see the opening, you are already there.
The opening right in front of you is the one you walk past most.
They get the future you are building and less of you today.
The doors you walk through are ones most people only look at.
The bad bets cost you the money the dull ones would have kept.
Their peace of mind rises and falls with your next move.
In a good year, everyone at your table eats well.
Your own cushion never gets the chance to grow.
Nobody near you ever doubts where your heart is.
Some of your best work exists only because someone else was ahead.
Your private hopes gather dust while the public races get all of you.
Your friends get faster just from standing next to you.
The wins you land are big enough to change your year.
One bad call takes years of savings with it, and you feel every pound.
Your partner lives through every swing beside you.
Everyone who stood beside you walks away feeling counted.
Offers go to the names people know, and yours is often missing.
Praise from you says little about who did what.
A worried room goes quiet soon after you sit down in it.
Some part of you is still waiting for someone to ask how you are.
They never get the chance to look after you in return.
People bring you their trouble because your advice holds up.
By the time you trust a thing, the first gains belong to someone else.
Their plans leave your hands sturdier than they came in.
Whatever someone learns from you, they learn without shame.
Your own work waits at the back of the queue.
They end up knowing your answer without the work of finding it.
People build their plans on what you say.
Your life slowly fills with old yeses made by a younger you.
Whatever you promised them still arrives, on time and in full.
People who lose to you still shake your hand.
A clean conscience matters to you more than any title.
Your own people sometimes wanted a champion and got a referee.
Around you, everyone knows what good looks like.
Your best days still feel like falling short.
Your group works to a mark it had no say in choosing.
Under your hands, old things keep earning their place.
Your weekends go to mending things worth less than the time they take.
Your family seldom gets to pick something new for themselves.
A bad month never finds you short.
Year after year, the treats you promised yourself stay on the list.
Whatever comes, your family has something to fall back on.
The people you stand by know exactly where to find you.
Under it all, you want proof that the bond runs both ways.
Those you love rarely hear it in words.
Your progress belongs to you and needs nobody's approval.
Every hard stretch, you climb with nobody beside you.
The people near you are measured against a line they cannot see.
In a bad week, you are the one still on your feet.
Underneath, you want someone to catch you for a change.
The help others would gladly give you stays unused.
People lean on you because you are the same on Monday as on Friday.
The comfort you give everyone else rarely comes back to you.
Beside you, a frightened friend finds solid ground.
The people around you are looked after before they feel the lack.
Underneath, you want to be wanted for more than what you bring.
They rarely get to say what they need from you.
Your work is still in daily use long after the fashion has moved on.
Rougher versions reach people before yours do, and the praise goes with them.
They manage without for a year while your careful version takes shape.
There is a peace in your home that money rarely buys.
Raises and roles you never pushed for go to people who did.
Those in your care grow up without the itch of always wanting more.
